resolvedQuestions.text: What does each runtime's prepare text tell the sender about keeping details out of the note, and does it over-promise what a fresh session can recover through the History Lookup?
What does the prepare text each runtime gives the sender say, and where does it let the sender drop a detail the receiver must later recover?
What claim text and History Lookup offer does the receiver read, and why would a receiver skip the lookup and ask the operator instead?
What claim text and History Lookup offer does the receiver read on OpenCode versus Pi, and what makes a receiver leave a claim unverified instead of running the lookup?
How do the OpenCode and Pi session readers feed the History Lookup, and do they redact secrets in tool-call argument shapes?
How do the OpenCode and Pi session readers feed the History Lookup, including their tool-call argument shapes and secret redaction, and what does each fail to recover?
Does model and effort carry on relaunch for each runtime, and where can it silently degrade or be dropped?
Does model and reasoning effort carry across the relaunch on each runtime, and what breaks when it does not?

Which known limits (OpenCode store without a directory column, AI_SESSION_CHILD leaking into test sandboxes, the 160-character preview cut, a double nudge from two hooks) cause a hop to fail, and what concrete fix addresses each?

keyFindings.text: Every runtime's prepare text is the same shared string, and it never mentions the History Lookup. `handoffText` lists the note shape (Goal, Done, Remaining work, In-flight state), the continuity save, the fan-out/lock release, and `prepare`/`keep`, and ends with the "skip these steps only when the operator said not to hand off" exception. No line names the lookup, so a sender has no way to learn that a detail kept out of the note is still recoverable. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:193]

keyFindings.text: The prepare nudge text enumerates the note's frontmatter shape and every required section, and never mentions the History Lookup. A sender reading it learns only that the note is the carrier, so a detail deliberately kept out of the note reads as a detail the hop loses. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:180]

The claim-seed text, which is the receiver's first instruction set, also has no lookup step. Its ordered steps are claim, read, resume, goal, `goal.md`, active command, continue Remaining work, complete — the offer is only whatever the `claim` command happens to print after the note body. A receiver that follows the seed literally can finish without ever opening the lookup. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:296]

keyFindings.text: The `prepare` command's only stdout is the arming line: `[session-handover] handoff prepared; stop now and end this turn.` plus the note path. It names no recovery path either, so the sender's last instruction before it stops carries the same omission. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/bin/session-handover.cjs:630]

The Pi 4/5 note carries an explicit false instruction written by the sender: "Ask the operator for it rather than inventing one, and say plainly that a fresh session cannot recover it from this note." That is the sentence the receiver obeyed. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/note-20261116T053237Z-01a1e2d7-6b7b-75de-a705-ee16233b97a3.md:28]

keyFindings.text: The Pi sender's note turned that omission into a false claim about the hop: `Ask the operator for it rather than inventing one, and say plainly that a fresh session cannot recover it from this note.` The sentence is true of the note and false of the hop, because the claim prints a working lookup. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/note-20261116T053237Z-01a1e2d7-6b7b-75de-a705-ee16233b97a3.md:31]

The OpenCode sender's note pointed the other way: `the side word recovered from the sender's earlier turn through the claim's History Lookup section. The note does not carry the side word by instruction.` Same withholding instruction, opposite instruction to the receiver, and that run scored 5/5. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-opencode/note-20261116T052759Z-ses_e1d2c7c81ffeJTAeWEY1UQO3wn.md:25]

The sender's recorded reasoning shows the over-promise is caused by missing knowledge, not by a careless claim: it reasoned "The claim seed carries only the note path and the spec folder. Hmm, does the seed carry anything else? ... So literally impossible", and then wrote the note accordingly. The sender had read only the first 175 lines of the README, so it never saw the History Lookup section at line 198. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/pane.txt:273]

keyFindings.text: The claim seed text tells the receiver `1. Run <claim>; it prints the note body.` and then walks it through the note's sections, the goal, the active command and completion. It never names the History Lookup, so the only place the offer appears is the claim command's own stdout, after the note body. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:276]

The offer was in fact printed to the Pi receiver, complete with a runnable `browse` command and the sentence "Use it for a detail this note does not spell out, before you guess." The receiver's own session log contains the rendered `## History Lookup` section, so this is not a minting failure, a store failure, or a transaction failure. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:1072]

keyFindings.text: The claim output appends the lookup section with the instruction `Use it for a detail this note does not spell out, before you guess.` That is a weaker directive than the note's own `Ask the operator for it`, and the note body is printed first, so the note's claim wins the reading order. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/bin/session-handover.cjs:729]

The Pi receiver then asserted the opposite of what the lookup could do: "A fresh session has no path to it — not through the note, not through history lookup, since it was never written." The side word had been written, in the sender's first user turn, which is exactly what the offered `browse` reads. A generic offer that arrives after a note which says "cannot recover" loses to the note. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/pane.txt:330]

The OpenCode note told the receiver to recover the side word "from the sender's earlier turn through the claim's History Lookup section", and that receiver ran the lookup, loaded the sender's first user turn, and quoted it. Both senders received the same shared prepare text; only the OpenCode sender had read far enough into the README to know the lookup existed. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-opencode/note-20261116T052759Z-ses_e1d2c7c81ffeJTAeWEY1UQO3wn.md:22]

keyFindings.text: The Pi receiver's reply shows the note's claim beating the offer: `A fresh session has no path to it — not through the note, not through history lookup, since it was never written.` It named the lookup and dismissed it on the note's authority, then asked the operator and left the note `claimed`. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/pane.txt:331]

The receiver's completion is never gated on the note's claims having been checked, so a false note claim survives to `complete`. On Pi the note stayed `claimed` only because the operator was asked; nothing in the protocol required the lookup to be tried first. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:340]

keyFindings.text: **Mode A — the sender is never told the lookup exists.** The prepare seed's opening line and the prepare stdout both describe writing a note and nothing else; neither names the History Lookup. A sender that believes the note is the only channel writes a closing sentence ("a fresh session cannot recover it") instead of a pointer. Fix: add one sentence to the prepare seed and to the prepare stdout naming the lookup and the fact that the receiver can read the sender's turns. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:180] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/bin/session-handover.cjs:630]

**Mode J — the scorecard can report a pass that did not happen.** The recall check slices at the last `[session-handover]` marker or the whole pane; the Pi pane has no marker, so `sideWordStated: true` is the sender's own prompt echo at character 12,812 of 30,172. The harness also plants no token and `score.cjs` has no redaction field. Fix: require the marker, or slice from the receiver's first turn, and add a token plant plus a redaction assertion. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/score.cjs:74] [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/live-hop.sh:61]

**Mode B — the note outranks the lookup in the claim text.** The claim seed omits the lookup, and the claim output prints the offer after the note body with a weaker directive, so a receiver that reads top-down treats the note as authoritative. The Pi receiver did exactly that: it dismissed the lookup on the note's authority and asked the operator. Fix: print the lookup offer before the note body and phrase it as a step, not an option. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:276] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/bin/session-handover.cjs:729]

**Mode C — a withheld offer is indistinguishable from no need to look.** `mintHandoverLocator` returns null on six conditions and the claim command wraps the call in a bare `catch {}`, so a withheld offer prints nothing, logs nothing and leaves no marker. Fix: return a typed refusal, print one line naming why the offer was withheld, and log it. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:929] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/bin/session-handover.cjs:729]

**Mode D — the OpenCode reader can return another project's session.** When the store has no `directory` column the reader skips the project proof, so the lookup's answer may come from a different checkout. Fix: require the column, or fall back to a cwd proof taken from the session's own record rather than from the store schema. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/hooks/shared/session-readers/opencode.mjs:256]

**Mode E — a secret survives redaction in three shapes.** `SECRET_ARGUMENT_KEY` misses `x-api-key` and `X-Api-Key`, the array branch of `redactArgument` drops the key, and image blocks are returned unchanged. Fix: accept a vendor prefix and a plural suffix in the key pattern, pass the parent key into the array branch, and document the image exclusion as a known limit rather than a guarantee. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:56] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:71] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:86]

**Mode F — a detail past character 160 is invisible until the receiver loads the turn.** The preview is the first 160 characters of redacted text, so a detail at character 295 of a 425-character turn appears in neither the preview nor any marker. The OpenCode receiver succeeded only because it chose to `load` the turn. Fix: raise the preview bound, or append an explicit "more at part N" handle so the receiver knows the preview is truncated. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/pages.ts:300]

**Mode G — model and effort do not carry on OpenCode.** `resolveSessionSettings` has no Pi or OpenCode branch, the OpenCode plugin never reads model or effort, `effort_is_valid` and `append_effort_arguments` have no OpenCode case, and `build_relaunch_arguments` drops the model on OpenCode 2. Pi is unaffected because its extension supplies the values itself. Fix: write the model and effort into the OpenCode config or a per-session setting, since the wrapper's own comment records that OpenCode 2 has no model flag on its root command. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:1121] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:775] [SOURCE: .pi/extensions/session-handover.ts:461]

**Mode H — the nudge is suppressed by a bare environment variable, and two hooks can both nudge.** `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` short-circuits `nudgeDecision` through `relaunchSessionIsChild`, a bare env read, so a test sandbox that inherits the variable gets no nudge at all. Separately, only claude, codex and vibe route through `commitNudge`; Pi and OpenCode keep in-process state, so two hooks can both nudge. Fix: replace the bare env read with a marker written into the relaunch environment, and route Pi and OpenCode through the same claim guard. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:707] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/hooks/context-nudge.mjs:157] [SOURCE: .pi/extensions/session-handover.ts:652] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/session-handover.js:181]

**Mode I — a claimed note never expires, so the sender's task is left open.** `completeHandoff` requires status `claimed`, `noteState` has no expired or abandoned state, no sweep expires a claimed note, and `questionHoldReason` covers only question tools, so a receiver that asks in prose holds the note open indefinitely. Fix: add an expiry sweep for a claimed note past its window, and widen the hold guard to a prose ask. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:407] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/killer.cjs:317] [SOURCE: .pi/extensions/session-handover.ts:188]

Redaction runs once, in the core, before projection: `redactHistoryEntries` maps every entry's content through `redactBlock`, so search, previews, part lists and pages all read already-redacted text. A route cannot reach an unredacted byte. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:101]

Tool-call arguments that are not a plain object are silently replaced with `{}`. `toolCallBlock` keeps arguments only when they are a non-array object, and the projection's `validBlock` requires an object; a runtime that stores a tool call's arguments as a JSON string yields a block that renders as the tool name plus `{}`, so the path, command or figure inside it is unrecoverable while the turn still looks intact. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/project.mjs:40]

An OpenCode store without a `directory` column cannot prove which folder a session ran in, and the reader does not fail closed. It selects `id` alone, and the folder check only runs when `hasDirectory` is true, so the session is accepted whatever folder it came from. The claim's mint then treats that acceptance as proof, which means the "note folder and recorded folder are in the same checkout" invariant is unenforced on exactly the stores the charter names. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/opencode.mjs:256]

`redactArgument` redacts a string argument only when its key matches `SECRET_ARGUMENT_KEY`; every other string falls through to `redactText`, which is a pattern scan of the value alone. The key rule is therefore the only thing that catches a short credential. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:71]

A projection defect is reported as `store_unreadable`, which misdiagnoses the cause and costs the whole session. One orphaned, duplicated or mismatched tool result makes `projectEntries` fail, and `readSession` converts any projection failure into `store_unreadable` — the same code the README tells receivers means the store "is missing or could not be read". The receiver is told the store is broken when the real cause is one turn's pairing. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/index.mjs:127]

`SECRET_ARGUMENT_KEY` does not match a prefixed header name. `x-api-key` fails the anchored alternation, so its value is scanned as bare text and a short token survives. Verified by running the scrubber: `{"x-api-key":"sk-live-abc123"}` comes back unchanged. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:57]

Pi finds a historical session only by exact project directory plus exact header id plus matching header `cwd`, and refuses two candidates as `session_ambiguous` rather than guessing. That is the correct conservative behaviour, but it makes the note's `cwd` load-bearing: a note whose `cwd` differs from the directory Pi keyed the session under cannot be read at all, and the claim then offers no lookup. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/pi.mjs:222]

The scrubber's `credential-assignment` pattern requires a 20-character value, so a short token is invisible to text scanning even when the key is spelled out. Verified: `apiKey=sk-live-abc123` is unchanged while `apiKey=sk-live-abcdefghij1234567890` redacts. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/dist/parsing/secret-scrubber.js:120]

The lookup CLI reads through the projected path, so hook-injected messages never reach a receiver. `cli.ts` calls `readSession`, which returns only `items`; the raw `loadSession` envelope is the only path that carries `injected`, and it is not the one the lookup uses. A detail that arrived as an injected block rather than a user or assistant turn is outside the lookup's reach. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/cli.ts:406]

The Pi reader proves the session before reading it: it requires the header's `type` to be `session`, its `id` to equal the requested id, and `samePath(header.cwd, projectDir)`, returning `session_mismatch` on any failure. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/pi.mjs:242]

Redaction runs once, before projection, on text, thinking and tool-call arguments. Argument keys matching the credential pattern are replaced whole, and every other string goes through the shared scrubber plus URL-password and authorization-value patterns. The consequence is safe by construction — no route reaches a raw entry — but it also means redaction can only see a secret whose key or shape it knows; a secret carried as an opaque positional argument under a neutral key such as `command` survives unless a value pattern matches. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:56]

The OpenCode reader skips that proof when the store has no `directory` column. `hasDirectory` is false, the SELECT narrows to `id`, and the `projectDir` comparison is guarded by `hasDirectory`, so a same-id session from another project is accepted and its parts are served. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/opencode.mjs:256]

The 160-character preview cut hides the live case's side word from the offer's own primary command. `previewFor` slices a turn's text to 160 characters, and `browse` returns those previews; the side word in the Pi sender's first user turn sits at character 295 of a 425-character prompt, so a receiver that ran exactly the offered `browse` would see a preview that does not contain it. Only `load`, the second operation listed in the offer's "Also:" line, returns the full turn. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/navigator.ts:265]

The 160-character preview cut hides the very detail a lookup is for. The side word sits at character 295 of the 425-character sender turn, so a `search` preview ends 135 characters before it; only `load` or `page` reaches the value. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/pages.ts:300]

Search previews are centered on the match, but browse previews are not. `searchPreview` calls `excerptAround` with the matched token's offsets, so a search for an identifier shows it even deep in a turn; `browse` uses the leading slice. The offer leads with `browse`, which is the one operation that cannot center on a value the receiver does not already know. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/navigator.ts:284]

The OpenCode receiver's success came from doing exactly that: it reported that it "loaded the sender's first user turn" and quoted the sentence holding the side word, rather than reading a preview. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-opencode/pane.txt:22]

Model and effort did carry on the live Pi hop. The receiver's session header records a `model_change` to provider `llmgateway`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, and a `thinking_level_change` to `max`, matching the sender's launch flags. The receiver's session name `hoptest-base1-pi (2)` confirms the record was read on the same path. So the Pi 4/5 result is not a carry failure. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts:459]

`resolveSessionSettings` has branches for `claude`, `codex` and `cursor` only. Every other runtime, including `pi` and `opencode`, falls to `return none`, so the CLI-side prepare record carries no model and no effort for them. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:1121]

Pi closes that gap from its own extension: `liveSettings` reads `ctx.model.id`, `ctx.model.provider` and `pi.getThinkingLevel()`, and the arm path writes them onto the record. Pi therefore carries model, provider and effort. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts:461]

The scorecard's "unobservable" is a measurement gap, not a drop. Its carry check reads model, effort, name and provider out of the receiver process's argv, and it marks every field unobservable when the first launch's argv is a bare runtime name. Pi's process argv is exactly `pi`, so no flag is ever visible; the harness never reads the receiver's session header, which is where Pi records both values. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/score.cjs:60]

After a hop, nothing durable records what the relaunch actually used. `relaunch.log` gets `relaunch loopId=... reason=ready` with no model, provider, effort or name, and the relaunch record itself is consumed and removed. An operator therefore cannot audit carry from artifacts, and a silent drop is indistinguishable from a carried value in every file the hop leaves behind. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/relaunch.log:3]

The OpenCode plugin never reads a model or an effort. Its only model access is `input?.model?.limit?.context`, which sizes the context window; nothing is written to the record. [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/session-handover.js:575]
`effort_is_valid` has no `opencode:` case, so an OpenCode effort would be rejected even if one were recorded. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:216]

OpenCode 2 carries neither model nor effort, by design. The wrapper appends `-m` only when the runtime is not OpenCode 2, and the effort appender has branches for Claude, Codex and Pi only. A receiver therefore starts on the configured default, so the 5/5 OpenCode run matched the sender's model only because the default happened to be the same model. A parity score that compares outcomes across runtimes is not testing carry at all. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:778]
`append_effort_arguments` has cases for `claude`, `codex` and `pi` only, so no OpenCode relaunch ever receives a thinking level. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:405]

Pi spends the nudge level before the nudge is delivered. `message_end` both stores the held text in an in-memory `Map` and writes the new level through `writeState`; delivery happens later on `turn_end` or `agent_end`. A host reload, a crash, or a run that ends between hold and delivery loses the held text while the level stays spent, so that session is never nudged again at that level and falls back to auto-compaction with no hand-over. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts:594]

`build_relaunch_arguments` drops the model on OpenCode 2 by design: the comment records that OpenCode 2's root command has no model flag and a replayed `-m` would end the launch with a usage error, so `-m` is appended only on OpenCode 1. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:775]

The two Pi hooks cannot double-deliver, because the held text is deleted from the map before `sendMessage`. `turn_end` steers the text into the running loop and `agent_end` sends it as a follow-up; whichever fires first consumes the entry and the second finds nothing. The charter's "double nudge from two hooks" is therefore a duplicate-delivery guard that works, while the uncovered risk on Pi is loss, not repetition. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts:620]

OpenCode computes and delivers the nudge in two different hooks, and the pair is guarded only by record state. The `event` hook queues a nudge when an assistant message completes; `experimental.chat.system.transform` re-queues from `pendingUsage` and pushes the text, while `pendingNudge` and `handoffPending` suppress a second. But a session that claimed a note gets `claimedReminder` on every request until the note leaves `claimed`, and once its own fill crosses the threshold it also gets a fresh nudge to prepare a new note, so one system prompt can carry two instructions: close the claimed note, and prepare a hand-over. [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/session-handover.js:590]
Pi's relaunch appends `--provider`, `--model`, `--thinking` and the plan or build mode, so a Pi hop replays all three carried values. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:753]

Neither live run proved the carry: the Pi scorecard records `model: unobservable, effort: unobservable` and the OpenCode scorecard records `model: not-set, effort: not-set`. The OpenCode run passed 5/5 because the harness launched both sessions on the same default, not because the model carried. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-opencode/scorecard.json]

`live_model_voids_launch_effort` deliberately drops the launch effort when the live model differs and brings no usable effort of its own, because some models reject an effort chosen for another. That rule is correct and is not the OpenCode gap. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:312]

`AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` short-circuits `nudgeDecision` before the ratio, the loop check and the level: `if (relaunchSessionIsChild(env)) return quiet('child-session')`. A sandbox that inherits the value gets no nudge at any fill. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:707]

The child flag is a single environment string comparison, and it is the first gate in the nudge decision. `relaunchSessionIsChild` returns true only when `AI_SESSION_CHILD` is exactly `1`, and `nudgeDecision` returns `child-session` before it looks at the fill ratio, the threshold, the hop cap or any record. A leaked flag therefore does not weaken the nudge; it removes it. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/goal/lib/goal-core.cjs:1191]

`relaunchSessionIsChild` is a bare environment read: `String(env[CHILD_SESSION_ENV] ?? '').trim() === '1'`. Nothing distinguishes a real dispatched child from a test process that inherited the variable, so the suppression cannot be narrowed from inside the decision. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/goal/lib/goal-core.cjs]

The wrapper does not scrub `AI_SESSION_CHILD` from the environment it launches a runtime with. Its unset lists cover `SKILLED_LOOP_*`, `SESSION_HANDOVER_GOAL_PACKET` and `SKILLED_LOOP_CLAIM_SEED`; the child flag is not among them, so a receiver inherits it from whatever launched the wrapper. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:911]

The live-hop harness unsets loop and Claude variables but not the child flag, so a harness run started from a dispatched worker produces a sender that is never nudged. The launch line unsets `SKILLED_LOOP_HOPS`, `SKILLED_LOOP_ID`, `CLAUDECODE` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, then adds the runtime-specific `unset_envs`; `AI_SESSION_CHILD` is absent from both lists. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/live-hop.sh:63]

The suppression is deliberate and correct for its purpose: a dispatched child owns no hand-over, and a nudge there would ask a worker to save continuity into the parent's packet, which is the write its brief forbids. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:703]

The base1 runs prove the leak was absent there, not that it is impossible. Both senders were nudged and prepared, which cannot happen with the flag set, so those two runs started from a shell that did not carry it. A rerun from inside a dispatched worker, a deep-research executor or a fan-out child would measure a session that never hands over. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/relaunch.log:1]

The packet's completion criterion therefore runs the history engine, hooks vitest, session readers and handover suites under `env -u AI_SESSION_CHILD`, which is the only way to get a nudge-capable environment from inside a child session. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/goal.md:62]

`commitNudge` is the double-nudge guard: it takes a per-session claim, re-runs `nudgeDecision` under that claim, writes the level, and releases in a `finally`. Two hooks racing therefore produce one delivery, because the loser re-decides against the level the winner wrote. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs]

The damage is asymmetric: the sender loses the nudge, but the claim path does not check the flag. `seedInstructions` parses the seed and builds the claim text with no child check, so a receiver that inherits the flag still receives and can still claim a note. The leak therefore breaks the start of a hop, not the claim of one already started. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:389]

Only three adapters use it: `claude/context-nudge.mjs`, `codex/shared.mjs` and `vibe/handover-parts.mjs`. Pi and OpenCode call `nudgeDecision` directly and never take the claim. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/claude/context-nudge.mjs:157]

Pi's substitute guard is the in-process `heldNudges` map, and `deliverHeldNudge` deletes the entry before sending, so `turn_end` followed by `agent_end` cannot deliver the same text twice within one process. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts:652]

OpenCode's substitute guard is `state.pendingNudge`, also in-process: `queueNudge` returns early when it is set. A plugin reload or a second host instance starts with it null and can deliver again. [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/session-handover.js:181]

The two-hook shape the claim exists for is real on Claude: `context-nudge.mjs` is registered on both `UserPromptSubmit` and `PostToolUse`, so one turn that submits a prompt and then runs a tool reaches the nudge code twice. [SOURCE: .claude/settings.json:169]

**Sender over-promise.** Change `handoffText` in `.skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs` to state that a detail kept out of the note is still recoverable by the receiver through the claim's History Lookup, and to forbid the sender from writing that a fresh session cannot recover it. Observable: a hop whose note deliberately omits a value no longer contains an "unrecoverable" instruction, and the receiver recovers the value. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:193]

The scorecard's recall check is `afterSeed.includes(meta.sideWord)`, where `afterSeed` is the pane from the last `[session-handover]` marker, or the whole pane when no marker exists. A pane with no marker therefore passes on the sender's own prompt echo. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/score.cjs:74]

**OpenCode 2 starts on the default.** There is no model flag to replay, so emit one warning line when the receiver's effective model differs from the sender's, and state the limitation in the runtime matrix. Observable: an OpenCode 2 hop that changed model prints the warning instead of passing silently. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:778]

**Pi loses a held nudge.** Persist the held text, or defer the `writeState` level bump until delivery, in `.skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts`, and deliver any held text on the next `agent_settled`. Observable: a host reload between hold and delivery still produces the nudge. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts:594]

**The child flag leaks.** Unset `AI_SESSION_CHILD` in `skilled-loop` before launching a runtime and in the live-hop harness's `tmux` line, so the flag describes the worker that owns it and never the session it launches. Observable: a hop started from a dispatched worker still nudges, prepares and claims. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:911]

**No verification step in the seed.** Add one step to `seedText` before "Continue the work": when Remaining work names a detail the note does not carry, run the printed History Lookup before asking the operator or closing the note. Observable: the receiver's transcript shows a `history-lookup.mjs` call before any operator question. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs:296]

The Pi pane contains no `[session-handover]` marker at all, so its `afterSeed` is the entire 30,172-character capture, and the side word appears at character 12,812 inside the echoed sender prompt. The Pi `sideWordStated: true` is that echo, not a receiver statement. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/pane.txt:149]

**The offer loses to the note.** Add one sentence to `buildHistoryLookupBody` in `.skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/lookup-offer.ts`: the note is not authoritative about what the sender's history holds, so try the lookup before concluding a detail is unrecoverable. Observable: a receiver facing a note that says "cannot recover" runs the lookup instead of repeating the note's claim. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/lookup-offer.ts:82]

The OpenCode pane's last marker sits at character 425, so its `afterSeed` starts after the seed and its side word is genuinely in the receiver's reply, which quotes the loaded turn. The OpenCode recall is real; the Pi one is not. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-opencode/pane.txt:22]

**Preview cut.** Make `browse` previews carry the whole first part up to the reply budget, or attach an explicit `load` pointer to every reference in the browse reply. Observable: the live prompt's side word at character 295 appears in a browse reply without a second call. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/navigator.ts:265]

The Pi receiver's own words contradict its scorecard: `A fresh session has no path to it — not through the note, not through history lookup, since it was never written.` The recall failed and the card recorded a pass. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/pane.txt:331]

**Arguments dropped by shape.** Change `toolCallBlock` in `.skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/project.mjs` to preserve a string argument, for example by parsing JSON or keeping it under a value key, instead of replacing it with `{}`. Observable: a session whose tool input is a JSON string returns the input in a loaded turn. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/project.mjs:40]

The Pi 4/5 is the `noteClosed` step, not the recall block: the note's status stayed `claimed` because the receiver held the close open waiting for the operator's answer. The recall block is scored apart from the five steps, so a failed recall cannot lower the score. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/scorecard.json]

**One bad pair costs the session.** Give projection defects their own refusal code and skip the offending pair instead of failing the read, in `projectEntries` and the dispatcher's `readSession` mapping. Observable: a session with one orphaned tool result still returns every other turn, and the refusal code names the pairing rather than the store. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/index.mjs:127]

The harness plants no token. `live-hop.sh` contains no `token`, `REDACT` or `plant` reference, so the packet's `[REDACTED:` completion criterion has no evidence from either run. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/live-hop.sh]

**Folder proof on OpenCode.** When the session table has no `directory` column, fail closed at mint (`readerFindsSession`) or record the folder on the locator at arm time and verify it against store metadata, in `.skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/opencode.mjs`. Observable: a note from another folder gets no lookup offer rather than another project's turns. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/opencode.mjs:256]

The carry block reports `unobservable` when the first launch line's basename equals the runtime and the line is exactly the runtime name, which is the Pi case, so Pi's carry can never be scored from the card even when it works. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/score.cjs:55]

**Pi cwd keying.** Record the Pi store key on the locator at mint and fall back to an exact-id scan of project directories when the note's `cwd` misses, in `.skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/pi.mjs`. Observable: a session started in a subdirectory is still found when the note records a later cwd. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/pi.mjs:222]

**Carry cannot be audited.** Append one `relaunch-args` line to `relaunch.log` from `skilled-loop` with model, provider, effort and name, and have `score.cjs` read a Pi receiver's session header for the same fields. Observable: `carry` reads `kept` or `dropped`, never `unobservable`. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:744]

`completeHandoff` throws unless the note's status is exactly `claimed`. A note in any other state cannot be completed, and a claimed note can only be completed by whoever holds it. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs]

**The five questions were answered from two very different evidence classes, and the guard was right to block.** Four questions (prepare text, readers, carry, known limits) rest primarily on production source code, which is one class. Only the claim-offer question rests on the runtime's own recorded state: the Pi note, the Pi pane, the receiver's session store and the scorecard. A stop justified by code reading alone is a single-lens claim, and the blocked stop named exactly that. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:653]

`noteState` accepts exactly `missing`, `invalid`, `open`, `claimed` and `done`. There is no `expired` or `abandoned` state, so a claim that is never closed has no representation other than `claimed`. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:407]

**The evidence base is stronger than the earlier iterations' prose suggested, once the classes are recorded.** Three independent primary artifacts agree on the 4/5 case: the sender's note contains the false "cannot recover" instruction, the sender's pane shows the reasoning that produced it, and the receiver's own session store contains the rendered lookup offer plus a reply that denies the lookup works. Those are three artifacts from two processes, not one file read twice. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/pane.txt:330]

Nothing expires a claimed note. The only stale sweeps in the handover code belong to the killer and cover lock files and takeover mutexes, not handoff notes. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/killer.cjs:317]

**Two questions still carry an inference, and the ledger makes that visible.** The Pi mid-session `cwd` hazard and the OpenCode two-instruction prompt are code-path conclusions with no live instance in `scratch/runs/`. They are recorded as secondary-class evidence and should not be counted as observed failures in synthesis. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/shared/session-readers/pi.mjs:222]

`questionHoldReason` blocks a question only while the session's record is armable, and the Pi extension applies it to two tool names: `question` and `ask_user_question`. A receiver that asks in prose is never blocked. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/pi/session-handover.ts:188]

The Pi receiver asked in prose: `So: what was the side word? Once you give it, I'll close the note.` The guard therefore never fired, and the note stayed `claimed` with the close deferred to an answer that could not arrive. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/pane.txt:333]

The claim output's completion instruction is conditional: `When the remaining work is done, run <complete> to close this note.` A note whose Remaining work requires an operator answer makes completion unreachable in an unattended run, and the receiver is following the instruction exactly. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/bin/session-handover.cjs:742]

The guard's own text already names the correct behaviour: end the turn and put the question in the handoff note for the next session, or cancel the hand-over first. The Pi receiver did neither, and nothing detected that. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/nudge.cjs]

**Only `ANSWERS` edges count toward source diversity; `SUPPORTS` edges do not.** `buildAnsweringFindingsByQuestion` skips every relation except `ANSWERS` before it collects cited sources. The iteration-6 ledger had recorded the Pi note and pane as a `SUPPORTS` relation to the prepare-text question, so its two primary artifacts never entered the class count even though they were cited. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:339]

`shouldRelaunch` declines with one of six named reasons: `no-file`, `not-armed`, `withdrawn`, `stale`, `hop-cap` and `incomplete-record`. Only a record that passes every check returns `{ relaunch: true }` with no reason. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs]

A record armed in the future is read as `stale`, not fresh, because a clock that stepped back makes the record's age unknown and stale is the safe reading. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs]

**Both blocked questions had their primary evidence filed one relation too weak.** The Pi note and pane answer what the prepare text failed to teach, and the measured 295-versus-160 offset answers what the browse reader fails to return. Recording them as answering findings raises each question to two classes without changing a conclusion or adding a source. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/navigator.ts:265]

The hop count is read as stored and never coerced, so a malformed or hand-edited record cannot slip under the cap by turning `null` into `0` or `"3"` into `3`. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs]

The wrapper calls `should-relaunch` only after the runtime process exits, and a non-zero status takes the decline path, which preserves the runtime's own exit code rather than replacing it. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:1263]

The killer's transcript grace is 1000 ms: a transcript that stays missing for one second makes `waitForIdle` return false, which un-arms the session, so no signal is sent and no hop happens. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/killer.cjs:23]
The killer's default timeout is 30000 ms. A session that never goes idle within that window is left running and the hop does not happen. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/killer.cjs:29]

`isLoopAncestor` throws on a failed process-table read, and the killer refuses to signal rather than guess at ancestry, so a process-table failure blocks the hop instead of risking a wrong kill. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/killer.cjs:220]

The Pi live run shows the path working end to end: prepare at 05:32:49.151, killer signal to pid 46361 at 05:32:57.828, relaunch at 05:32:58.064 with reason `ready`. The Pi failure was therefore downstream of the relaunch, not in it. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/runs/base1-pi/relaunch.log]

**A question counts as covered only when at least two findings answer it directly.** Coverage is `(questions with >= 2 ANSWERS edges) / total questions`, so a question with one strong answer and three supporting findings still counts as uncovered. The lineage had two such questions: the claim-offer question had no `ANSWERS` edge at all (its evidence was filed as `SUPPORTS`), and the known-limits question had one. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:570]

The CLI refuses a locator older than 30 minutes: `LOCATOR_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`, and `isFresh` requires `ageMs >= 0 && ageMs < LOCATOR_TTL_MS`. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/cli.ts:37]
A locator whose `mintedAt` is in the future counts as stale, because a future timestamp is clock skew rather than freshness. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/cli.ts:217]

**The same relation error depressed the diversity average, not the evidence base.** `sourceDiversity` is the mean distinct quality classes per question over all question nodes, so a question with no answering finding contributes zero even when its primary artifacts are recorded and cited. Filing the direct answers raises both signals at once: coverage from 0.6 to 1, and the diversity mean from 1.4 to 2. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:653]

The mint is done at claim time rather than at prepare time precisely because of that TTL, so a note claimed hours after it was written still redeems. This is the correct design and is not a failure mode. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:1060]

`mintHandoverLocator` returns null, and therefore withholds the offer, on any of: an empty runtime or session id, a runtime with no locator kind, a transcript-based runtime with no transcript path, a `placeLookup` miss, a reader that cannot find the session, or a recorded folder outside the sender's checkout. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:929]

For Pi and OpenCode the mint asks the reader directly (`readerFindsSession`) instead of resolving a transcript path, so the mint and the lookup agree on whether the session exists. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:929]

The offer is withheld unless the receiver's workspace and the sender's workspace are the same checkout, because the printed command moves to the locator's workspace and would otherwise read the wrong repository. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:1090]

`lookupRunsFrom` requires three things in the workspace: a `.git` entry, the entry script, and the compiled core at `.skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/dist/cli.js`. A checkout without a built core gets no offer at all. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/lookup-offer.ts]

Every one of those conditions fails closed by returning null, and the claim command wraps the call in a bare `catch {}`, so a withheld offer produces no message, no log line and no marker in the claim output. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/bin/session-handover.cjs:729]

Redaction runs before projection: `createHistoryLookup` calls `projectHistoryEntries(redactHistoryEntries(entries), options)`, so every preview, page offset, part list and search index is computed on the text a caller receives. A secret therefore cannot be matched by `search`, and a secret straddling a page boundary is redacted before the boundary is chosen. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:136]

keyFindings.text: The shared scrubber is shape-driven, not entropy-driven. It requires a vendor prefix, a fixed length, or an assignment context with both a digit and a letter and a 20-character floor. A generic plant such as `FAKE_TOKEN_abc123` or `PLANTED_FAKE_TOKEN_9f3a2b1c8d7e6f5a` passes through unchanged. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/parsing/secret-scrubber.ts:59] [SOURCE: verified by running `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/dist/parsing/secret-scrubber.js` on both strings; both returned unchanged]
sources: Compiled scrubber run over seventeen candidate strings and seven header/URL shapes

keyFindings.text: A realistic-looking fake key can still miss. `sk-fake-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef` misses the OpenAI pattern because the hyphen after `sk-` breaks the base62 value class, and `AIzaFake0123456789abcdef0123456789abc` misses the Google pattern because its tail is 33 characters against a required 35. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/parsing/secret-scrubber.ts:102] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/parsing/secret-scrubber.ts:109] [SOURCE: verified by running the compiled scrubber on both strings; both returned unchanged]

keyFindings.text: `SECRET_ARGUMENT_KEY` does not match `x-api-key` or `X-Api-Key`, because the alternation requires the key to begin with `api`, `access`, `auth`, `client`, `refresh` or `secret`. The value alone carries no assignment context, so `{"x-api-key": "FAKE0123456789abcdef"}` leaks both the key and the value. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:56] [SOURCE: verified by running the `SECRET_ARGUMENT_KEY` and `redactText` patterns on the header shape; both returned unchanged]

keyFindings.text: The array branch of `redactArgument` drops the key: `value.map((item) => redactArgument(item))` passes no key, so a plural secret key holding an array is not redacted by key and each item is only shape-scanned. `{"api_keys": ["plainpassphrase"]}` survives. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:71]

keyFindings.text: `redactBlock` returns image blocks unchanged, deliberately, because image bytes are base64 where a pattern hit would corrupt the image. A token visible in a screenshot is therefore not redacted, and the criterion cannot be met by planting the token in an image. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/core.ts:86]

[SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/live-hop.sh:61] [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/session-handover/001-history-lookup-handover-integration/011-opencode-pi-handover-parity/scratch/harness/score.cjs]

It does not cover `x-api-key`, plural keys, arrays under a secret key, or image blocks, so the guarantee is narrower than the test's name suggests. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/tests/history-secret-redaction.vitest.ts:15] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/tests/history-secret-redaction.vitest.ts:28]

keyFindings.text: The preview is the first 160 characters of already-redacted text, so a token past character 160 yields a reply containing neither the token nor a marker. The criterion is satisfiable only on a `load` or `page` reply, or with the token inside the first 160 characters of the turn. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/lib/pages.ts:300]

ruledOutDirections.text: Searching the prepare/seed text for any recovery wording: there is none to find. Any fix has to add it rather than repair it.

"The Pi session reader could not find the sender's session": ruled out indirectly; the claim mint calls the same reader and the mint succeeded, since the section printed. The remaining reader risk is therefore about breadth of what a found session yields, not about finding it.

Reading the pane transcript for the claim command's stdout. The capture collapses tool output, so the offer's presence cannot be proven or disproven from the pane. The code path plus the goal's recorded observation is the stronger evidence.
"The Pi sender leaked the side word." Both scorecards record `sideWordInNote: false`, so the withholding instruction held on both runtimes.
"Pi did not mint or print the lookup": ruled out by finding 5 — the receiver's session log holds the rendered section and a `hl1_` handle.
"The shared prepare text differs between OpenCode and Pi": ruled out; both adapters call the same `handoffText`.

"The Pi lookup was never offered." The packet goal records that the offer was printed and works, and `handoverLookupSection` mints the locator at claim time from the note's own `session_id`, `runtime` and `cwd`, all three of which the Pi note carries. The pane capture collapses tool output, so its silence is not evidence of absence. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-handover/lib/relaunch-core.cjs:1072]

"Fixing the prepare text alone would close the Pi gap." The Pi receiver had a working offer and did not run it, so the claim text and the note's authority are the binding constraint, not the prepare text.
